findings.title: Null list / null element produces raw NPE instead of a contract error
findings.evidence: The loop 'for (LineItem item : items) {' dereferences the caller-supplied list and each element without any guard, while LineItem's own constructor carefully throws IllegalArgumentException for bad input — the class is inconsistent about how it reports invalid input, and 'subtotal(null)' fails with an unexplained NullPointerException.
findings.recommendation: Validate up front: 'Objects.requireNonNull(items, "items required")' and reject null elements (or skip with a documented rule). If totals must be a point-in-time snapshot, copy the list before iterating so concurrent mutation cannot yield a partial subtotal.

findings.title: taxRate is unvalidated: null NPE, negative or >1 rates silently produce nonsense totals
findings.evidence: 'BigDecimal tax = cents(subtotal.multiply(taxRate));' multiplies by an unchecked rate, so null throws a bare NPE, a negative rate produces a negative tax line, and a caller passing a percentage (8.25) rather than a fraction (0.0825) yields an 825% tax with no error. The unit of taxRate is also undocumented.
findings.recommendation: Reject null via Objects.requireNonNull and reject rates outside [0, 1] with IllegalArgumentException, and document in Javadoc whether the rate is a fraction of the subtotal.

findings.title: Negative unitPrice accepted with no guard or explicit credit semantics
findings.evidence: Only null 'unitPrice' and non-positive quantity are rejected; a negative price (a plausible data-entry or import error) silently reduces the invoice total, and because HALF_UP rounds ties away from zero, those credit lines round to the larger magnitude rather than toward zero.
findings.recommendation: Either reject negative unitPrice in the compact constructor, or model credits as a separate field/kind and document the rounding behaviour for negative amounts.

findings.title: No test pins the rounding mode or the round-per-line-before-summing rule
findings.evidence: ROUNDING is a fixed policy constant and subtotal rounds each line before summing, but the change adds no tests; a later reorder (round only the final total) would change invoice amounts for sub-cent prices with no failing test to catch it.
findings.evidence_quote: private static final RoundingMode ROUNDING = RoundingMode.HALF_UP;
findings.recommendation: Add tests covering a half-cent tie (e.g. unit price 0.005, quantity 1 and 3), an empty list, many-line rounding drift versus a single final rounding, and a negative line, asserting the exact 2-decimal result and scale.
